newsitem.title: CHINA: China sees 1997 tourism income at $10.5 billion.
newsitem.headline: China sees 1997 tourism income at $10.5 billion.

text.p: China expects to earn $10.5 billion from foreign tourists in 1997, which it has declared the Year of Tourism, the Wen Hui Bao newspaper on Sunday quoted the head of the National Tourism Bureau as saying.
He Guangwei put arrivals from outside mainland China in 1997 at 49 million, including 6.6 million by foreigners. Most of the visitors are ethnic Chinese from Hong Kong, Macau and Taiwan.
The comparable figures in 1995 were 46.39 million visits earning $8.73 billion, ranking China ninth in the world in terms of foreign exchange earnings from tourism, He said.
He estimated 1997 earnings from tourism by mainland Chinese at 175 billion yuan, up from 137.57 billion in 1995. He gave no 1996 figures.
In 1997 there will be 48 tourism festivals in China as well as the return of Hong Kong to the motherland on July 1, all of which will help to promote tourism, he said without elaborating.
